title: Spatial transcriptomics analysis of normal lung tissues, precursor lung lesions and invasive lung adenocarcinomas
summary: Understanding cellular processes underlying early lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) development is needed to devise intervention strategies. Here, we performed spatial trancriptomics analysis of human treatment-naive lungs comprising various stages in the sequence of pathogenesis of LUAD including normal lung tissues, atypical adenomatous hyperplasia (AAH), adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS), minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (MIA) and LUAD.
overall_design:
Spatial transcriptomics analysis of samples was done using the Visium CytAssist platform from 10x Genomics. All tissues were surgically resected and formalin-fixed paraffin embedded.

title: Lung tissue with AAH of patient 1 [ST]
characteristics_ch1: cell line: Formalin-fixed paraffin embedded human lung tissue
data_processing:
Visium ST experiment: Demultiplexed reads were pre-processed using Space Ranger (v2.0.0, 10x Genomics) and aligned to the GRCh38 reference genome. ST profiling of human FFPE tissues from P1-P25 was performed using the CytAssist-enabled Visium platform with 11 x 11 mm fiducial frames (each frame comprises roughly 14,000 spots) from 10x Genomics according to the manufacturer’s recommendations. ST RNA-seq libraries were generated according to the manufacturer’s instructions with an average of ~11,000 uniquely barcoded spots/tissue. Libraries were sequenced on NovaSeq 6000 or NovaSeq X platforms (Illumina) to achieve an average depth of ~65,000 mean reads per spot and ~3,400 median genes per spot. The resulting unique molecular identifier (UMI) count matrices were analyzed using Seurat (v5.1.0) in the R platform. Spot-level histopathological annotation and visualization were generated using loupe browser (v.7.1). An experienced pathologist then checked and annotated each spot by using the Loupe Browser with the corresponding high-resolution images. Spots annotated as “Space”, "Foreign body", "Tissue artifacts" were filtered out during QC processing. 18Detailed QC metrics were generated and evaluated, and spots were carefully filtered to obtain high-quality data for downstream analyses. Briefly, for basic quality filtering, spots with nUMI < 500 and nFeature < 200 and relative high percentage of mitochondrial genes >15% were filtered out.
Assembly: GRCh38
Supplementary files format and content: images, tab-delimited text files include barcodes, features/genes, coordinates, and raw counts for each sample
Library strategy: Spatial transcriptomics

Visium ST experiment: Demultiplexed reads were pre-processed using Space Ranger (v2.0.0, 10x Genomics) and aligned to the GRCh38 reference genome. ST profiling of human FFPE tissues from P1-P25 was performed using the CytAssist-enabled Visium platform with 11 x 11 mm fiducial frames (each frame comprises roughly 14,000 spots) from 10x Genomics according to the manufacturer’s recommendations. ST RNA-seq libraries were generated according to the manufacturer’s instructions with an average of ~11,000 uniquely barcoded spots/tissue. Libraries were sequenced on NovaSeq 6000 or NovaSeq X platforms (Illumina) to achieve an average depth of ~65,000 mean reads per spot and ~3,400 median genes per spot. The resulting unique molecular identifier (UMI) count matrices were analyzed using Seurat (v5.1.0) in the R platform. Spot-level histopathological annotation and visualization were generated using loupe browser (v.7.1). An experienced pathologist then checked and annotated each spot by using the Loupe Browser with the corresponding high-resolution images. Spots annotated as “Space”, "Foreign body", "Tissue artifacts" were filtered out during QC processing. 18Detailed QC metrics were generated and evaluated, and spots were carefully filtered to obtain high-quality data for downstream analyses. Briefly, for basic quality filtering, spots with nUMI < 500 and nFeature < 200 and relative high percentage of mitochondrial genes >15% were filtered out.
Assembly: GRCh38
Supplementary files format and content: images, tab-delimited text files include barcodes, features/genes, coordinates, and raw counts for each sample
Library strategy: Spatial transcriptomics
